ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the first quadrant of the coordinate system, there are magnetic fields in regions I and II, with a magnetic induction strength of $B=1.0\mathrm{T}$, directed perpendicularly into the plane of the paper. In region I, there is a uniform electric field orthogonal to the magnetic field, with an electric field strength of $E=1.0\times10^{3}\mathrm{V/m}$, and the direction is unknown. A negatively charged particle with mass $m=1{\times}10^{-14}\mathrm{kg}$ and charge $q=1{\times}10^{-10}\mathrm{C}$ enters the first quadrant from point $O$ at a certain velocity $v$ at an angle of $53^{\circ}$ to the positive $x$-axis. It moves in a straight line in region I, then enters region II and exits from the right side. After some time, the particle passes through point $D$ on the $x$-axis (not shown in the figure). The coordinates of point $A$ are $(12\mathrm{cm},0)$, and the coordinates of point $C$ are $(26\mathrm{cm},0)$. Given that $\sin53^{\circ}=0.8$ and $\cos53^{\circ}=0.6$, the gravitational force on the particle is negligible.

1. What is the magnitude of the particle's velocity $v$?
2. Find the coordinates of the intersection point \( D \) of the particle's trajectory with the \( x \)-axis.
3. What is the time required to move from point $O$ to point $D$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a first-quadrant coordinate system, the horizontal axis is labeled x/cm, the vertical axis is labeled y/cm, and the origin is O. On the x-axis there are two vertical dashed-line boundaries, respectively passing through A and C, dividing the region in the first quadrant into I, II, and the right-side region. In regions I and II there are “×” marks drawn, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward. The particle enters from point O along an oblique upward-right direction making 53° with the positive x-axis, and the figure uses an arrow to mark this incident direction. Point A is at the intersection of the first dashed line and the x-axis, and point C is at the intersection of the second dashed line and the x-axis. According to the problem statement and method draft, the particle moves in a straight line in region I, so the resultant force of the electric field force and Lorentz force is zero: q(E+v×B)=0. Therefore the speed magnitude satisfies E=vB, namely v=E/B=(1.0×10^3)/(1.0)=1.0×10^3 m/s. Let the intersection point from region I to region II be P. A's x-coordinate is 12 cm, the incident straight line makes 53° with the x-axis, tan53°=sin53°/cos53°=0.8/0.6=4/3, so P's coordinates are x=12 cm, y=12×4/3=16 cm, namely P=(12 cm,16 cm). In region II there is only a magnetic field, and the particle undergoes uniform circular motion, with radius r=mv/(|q|B)=(1×10^-14×1×10^3)/(1×10^-10×1)=0.10 m=10 cm. For a negative charge in a magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface inward, according to the given method, the center of the circle is located in the lower-right normal direction of the incident velocity direction, 10 cm from point P. The component ratio of the incident velocity direction is (cos53°,sin53°)=(0.6,0.8), and the corresponding lower-right normal direction is (0.8,-0.6), so the center coordinates are (12+8,16-6)=(20 cm,10 cm). The circular trajectory equation is (x-20)^2+(y-10)^2=100, with units in cm. The particle leaves from the right boundary x=26 cm of region II. Substituting into the circular equation gives (26-20)^2+(y-10)^2=100, namely 36+(y-10)^2=100, so y=18 cm or 2 cm. The point first reached along the clockwise trajectory is Q=(26 cm,18 cm). At point Q, the tangent direction is perpendicular to the radius (6,8), and according to the direction of motion is (8,-6), therefore after leaving region II it moves along this straight line. From Q=(26,18) and slope -6/8=-3/4, the straight-line equation is y-18=-(3/4)(x-26). Let y=0, giving x-26=24, so x=50 cm. Therefore D=(50 cm,0). The time is calculated in three sections. OP=√(12^2+16^2) cm=20 cm=0.20 m, t1=0.20/1000=2.0×10^-4 s. The circular arc in region II corresponds to central angle 90°=π/2, arc length s2=rπ/2=0.10×π/2=0.157 m, t2=1.57×10^-4 s. QD=√(24^2+18^2) cm=30 cm=0.30 m, t3=0.30/1000=3.0×10^-4 s. The total time t=t1+t2+t3=(2.0+1.57+3.0)×10^-4=6.57×10^-4 s.
